A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NormBT research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original reward-model training experiments, RewardBench and Best-of-N evaluations, ablations, and five-seed results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, a BSR comparison, EMA sensitivity results, and a Skywork distance analysis.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same representation-distance weighting, stop-gradient treatment, EMA stabilization with default beta = 0.9, and weighted BT objective. The additional experiments do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Table 4 adds actual evaluations on RM-Bench, RewardBench-2, and Preference Proxy Evaluations. These substantially broaden evaluation coverage, including factuality, precise instruction following, ties, and named knowledge and coding tests. The original training datasets, RewardBench evaluation, and Best-of-N task remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 newly evaluates BT + Batch-wise Sum-to-zero Regularization (BSR), which v2 only discussed through its related-work citation. The existing BT, margin, margin-out, label-smoothing, LayerNorm, and gradient-clipping comparison methods remain represented.

E3.justification: New Table 3 evaluates EMA coefficients 0.70, 0.80, and 0.85 alongside the retained default 0.90, using gemma-2b-it and Unified-Feedback (80K). This adds a controlled parameter sweep; the existing main-training and Best-of-N protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds sensitivity testing of the EMA coefficient, and Figure 4 adds a Skywork-trained model comparison to the existing distance-binned diagnostic. The no-EMA, pooling, and cosine ablations and appendix analyses are retained; the separately reported clipping-at-3.0 result is omitted.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains five seeds per method on Unified-Feedback (40K), with identical standard-error reporting in Figure 5 and the table renumbered from 4 to 6. The new experiments provide point estimates without introducing additional run-count disclosures or uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: Table 4 substantially expands results: BT/NormBT aggregate scores are 57.87/58.98 on RM-Bench, 30.08/34.17 on RewardBench-2, and 50.82/51.33 on PPE, although some subcategories decline. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance changes between versions. v3 also adds BSR results, EMA-sweep scores, and Skywork distance-bin findings, while dropping the clipping-at-3.0 row. Table 1 and Appendix C scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The gradient derivation, Lipschitz-smoothness assumption, normalization mathematics, and baseline formulations in Equations 1–18 are unchanged. The added BSR discussion introduces no new formal definition or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central claims about representation-distance bias, NormBT's lightweight correction, and improved reward modeling, particularly for fine-grained distinctions. The conclusion's added emphasis on challenging tasks restates an existing abstract and introduction claim.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the BSR comparison as supporting pairwise update allocation and the EMA sweep as supporting coefficients around 0.8–0.9. Appendix A explicitly identifies noise amplification within its existing noisy-pair caveat. The principal mechanism explanation and downstream-evaluation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 2 removes explicit gradient-clipping thresholds: its remaining clipping row reproduces v2's 5.0 scores but no longer specifies the threshold. The EMA sweep documents its coefficient values and training setting. Appendix B's implementation, hardware, and training details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A new calibration paragraph cites Huang, Leng, Tao, and Halpern, and expands the distinction between NormBT and the already-cited BSR work. References for LayerNorm and gradient clipping are also added. This refines positioning without redefining the central contribution.

P1.justification: Analysis moves before the former Ablation Studies section, which becomes Additional Results. Related work expands, with localized abstract, conclusion, and limitations edits. Affiliations, conference front matter, and acknowledgements are updated; the main method narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is relocated and expanded with a Skywork panel. Table 2 gains descriptive group headings, and new Tables 3 and 4 display EMA and benchmark results. Appendix tables are renumbered, with localized resizing and spacing changes to retained displays.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmarks, closely related BSR comparison, EMA sensitivity study, and Skywork diagnostic strengthen empirical support for the unchanged central claims. Clearer research positioning also helps. These gains are limited by testing only one trained model pair on the added benchmarks without uncertainty estimates, while the clipping threshold disclosure is lost.
